verdict: Intel's revenue jumped 25% to $16.1B — its fastest growth in more than fifteen years — and the core business made $1.8B of operating profit, but a $12.5B paper charge on the U.S. government escrow shares turned the bottom line into a $10.8B net loss.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; strongest growth in over 15 years

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, attributable to Intel; non-GAAP EPS was $0.42

segments.name: Client Computing and Physical AI Group
segments.note: Chips for PCs and edge devices — still Intel's biggest business.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Server CPUs and AI accelerators for data centers — the growth engine this quarter.

segments.note: Chip manufacturing for outside customers only — most of Foundry's $5,765M of segment revenue is internal, making chips for Intel itself.

segments.note: Mobileye, IMS and smaller businesses; down YoY after the Altera sale in Sep 2025.

opex.note: Developing new CPUs, AI accelerators and process technology; down from $3,684M a year ago.

follow100.label: Client Computing and Physical AI Group

follow100Note: Other expense took $78.21 of every $100 — almost all of it the non-cash escrow-shares charge — which is how a profitable operating quarter ends as a $67.26 loss per $100. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Other expense of $12,615M combines a $39M loss on equity investments, net, with $12,576M of interest and other, net — and that line is dominated by a $12,529M mark-to-market loss on the U.S. government Escrowed Shares: as Intel's share price rose, the value of the shares Intel must hand over rose too, and accounting books that as a loss. It is a paper charge, not cash.
footerNote: Foundry is shown at its $288M of outside sales only (its $5,765M segment revenue is mostly internal; intersegment eliminations were -$5,477M). Net income attributable to Intel was a loss of $11,033M, after $185M of income attributable to non-controlling interests; the chart uses the total net loss of $10,848M.

takeaways.title: The core business is growing again
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 25% to $16,128M — Intel's strongest growth in over fifteen years — with Data Center and AI up 59% to $6,262M and client computing up 13%. Gross margin jumped to 40.4% from 27.5% a year ago, and operating income was $1,796M versus a $3,176M loss a year ago.

takeaways.title: A paper charge created the headline loss
takeaways.text: The $12,529M mark-to-market loss on the U.S. government Escrowed Shares is non-cash: Intel's rising share price increased the value of shares it owes the government under the CHIPS Act agreement. Excluding it and other items, non-GAAP net income attributable to Intel was a profit of about $2.2B (EPS $0.42).

takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed strong
takeaways.text: Intel generated $7.0B of cash from operations in the quarter despite the paper loss. For Q3 it guided revenue of $15.8B to $16.8B, while flagging heavier investment in equipment, clean-room space and substrates to support growth.

oneTimers: Mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares: $12,529M, inside 'interest and other, net' — a non-cash charge that rises when Intel's share price rises; Intel excludes it from non-GAAP results.
Restructuring and other charges were $170M in the quarter, mostly severance under the 2025 Restructuring Plan (versus $1,890M a year ago).
